mainTopic: Why a קונם on a wife's handiwork can take effect despite the husband's rights, and a new משנה about a husband who annuls a vow while mistaken about its details
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why שמואל ruled like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that a wife's קונם on her handiwork needs annulling. רב אשי says a קונם is different: it is treated like קדושת הגוף, holiness that sits on the object itself. He backs this with רבא's rule that הקדש, חמץ and freeing a slave all cancel a שעבוד (someone's claim on the item). So the wife's קונם overrides her husband's claim on her work and takes effect right away. The גמרא asks why, then, רבי יוחנן בן נורי gave the reason 'perhaps he will divorce her.' It answers that this is only an extra reason, read as 'and furthermore.' A new משנה then teaches that if a husband or father annulled a vow while mistaken about who vowed or what was vowed, he must annul it again. The גמרא opens its discussion by asking whether this means the פסוק's word אוֹתָהּ ('her') is meant exactly.

steps.title: רב אשי: קונמות are like inherent holiness
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new explanation: a קונם is different because it is treated like קדושת הגוף, and this fits רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: קונמות are different, because they are like holiness of the object itself, and this follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanations were not accepted, so רב אשי gives a new reason why the wife's קונם on her work can take effect. He says a קונם is as strong as holiness that sits on the object itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the wife's work already 'belongs' to her husband, so how can she forbid it? רב אשי answers that a קונם is not a weak prohibition; it is like קדושת הגוף. He points to רבא's rule, which the גמרא will quote next, to show that such strong holiness can cancel someone else's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows that forbid something like a קרבן (plural of קוּנָּם)
Holiness on the object itself, not just on its value

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying a קונם is actually הקדש. He is saying it is treated as strongly as קדושת הגוף.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Konamot are different,
for they are like inherent sanctity,
and this is in accordance with Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces earlier rejected explanations of why the wife's קונם takes effect.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the strength of a קונם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's claim on her work should stop her קונם from taking effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קונם is like קדושת הגוף, which is strong enough to override his claim.

steps.title: רבא's rule: Strong prohibitions cancel a lien
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught that הקדש, חמץ and freeing a slave cancel any שעבוד on the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא said: consecrating, חמץ, and freeing a slave all cancel a lien.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא's rule that רב אשי relied on. It shows that strong holiness or prohibitions can break someone else's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a lender has a claim on an item, making it הקדש, it becoming forbidden חמץ, or freeing the slave wipes out that claim. Since a קונם is like קדושת הגוף, it too wipes out the husband's claim on his wife's work.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving something to the בית המקדש
A lien, a claim someone has on property

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule is a well-known principle: strong holiness or prohibition overrides a creditor's claim.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
Consecration, leavened bread, and emancipation
cancel a lien.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'כדרבא' that רב אשי mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: That a קונם can override the husband's claim on her work
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule that הקדש, חמץ and שחרור cancel a שעבוד

steps.title: Then why mention 'perhaps he will divorce her'?
steps.stepSummary: If the קונם takes effect right away, why did רבי יוחנן בן נורי need the reason that the husband might divorce her?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need 'perhaps he will divorce her'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's approach. If the vow works now, the reason about a future divorce seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said the husband should annul because maybe he will divorce her, and then the vow would apply. That suggests the vow does not work now. But according to רב אשי, it works right away, so the divorce reason looks pointless.

phrases.english: If so, why do I need
'perhaps he will divorce her'?
phrases.notes: This is the reason רבי יוחנן בן נורי gave for why the husband should annul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's explanation using רבי יוחנן בן נורי's own wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the קונם takes effect immediately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reason based on future divorce implies the vow does not work now, which contradicts רב אשי.

steps.title: Read it as 'and furthermore, perhaps he will divorce her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the divorce reason is just an extra reason, added with 'and furthermore'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach: 'And furthermore, perhaps he will divorce her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the divorce reason as a second, extra reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main reason to annul is that the vow works right away. The divorce reason is added for anyone who thinks the husband's claim is strong enough to hold the vow back: even then, he should annul because he might divorce her.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, a קונם is like קדושת הגוף and cancels the husband's claim, so the vow works now; 'perhaps he will divorce her' is only an extra reason.

phrases.english: Teach: And furthermore, perhaps he will divorce her.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording as an additional reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorce reason is the only reason, implying the vow does not work now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The divorce reason is an extra reason; the vow does work now.

steps.title: משנה: Annulling a vow while mistaken
steps.stepSummary: If a husband annulled a vow while mistaken about who vowed or what was vowed, he must annul again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his wife vowed and he thought his daughter did, or the reverse; if she vowed to be a נזיר and he thought she vowed a קרבן, or the reverse; if she vowed off figs and he thought grapes, or the reverse — he must go back and annul again.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that an annulment made while mistaken about the vow does not work, and the husband (or father) must annul again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three kinds of mistakes: about who made the vow, about the type of vow, and about what item was forbidden. In each case his annulment was aimed at a different vow than the real one, so he must annul the real vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vows to avoid wine, haircuts and impurity
He must go back and annul again

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the vow is fully annulled; the first annulment did not work, so he must do it again.

phrases.english: MISHNA: His wife vowed
and he thought his daughter had vowed,
his daughter vowed and he thought his wife had vowed,
she vowed to be a nazirite and he thought she vowed an offering,
she vowed an offering and he thought she vowed to be a nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: נָדְרָה מִתְּאֵנִים וְסָבוּר שֶׁנָּדְרָה מִן הָעֲנָבִים,
phrases.english: she vowed off figs and he thought she vowed off grapes,

phrases.aramaic: נָדְרָה מִן הָעֲנָבִים וְסָבוּר שֶׁנָּדְרָה מִן הַתְּאֵנִים —
phrases.english: she vowed off grapes and he thought she vowed off figs —
he must go back and annul.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָדְרָה אִשְׁתּוֹ וְסָבוּר שֶׁנָּדְרָה בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An annulment made while mistaken about who vowed or what was vowed does not work; he must annul again.

steps.title: Is the word 'her' in the verse meant exactly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking whether the משנה's ruling shows that the word אוֹתָהּ in the פסוק must be read exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this mean that the words 'he annuls her' are meant exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a question. It asks what the משנה's rule tells us about how to read the פסוק, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if a man annulled a vow while thinking someone else made it, the annulment does not work. That sounds like the פסוק's word אוֹתָהּ ('her') is exact: he can annul only for the specific woman he means. The גמרא asks whether we really read the word that strictly, which hints that a challenge to this reading may follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
Is this to say that... (a question about what follows from a ruling)
He annuls her (words from the פסוק about a husband annulling his wife's vow)
Exactly or precisely, meaning the word is to be read strictly

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that 'he annuls her'
is precise?
phrases.notes: In other words, does 'her' mean he must have this specific woman in mind when he annuls?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the משנה's ruling in step 5 (annulment made by mistake must be redone) and asks what it shows about the wording of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's ruling shows that the word אוֹתָהּ in the פסוק must be read exactly, so that a husband can annul only for the specific woman he intends.
